text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London were tightly mixed in dull trade. August ended at $326 per tonne, unchanged from the previous close, while October added 70 cents to close at $316.70 per tonne. There was no fresh news to influence prices. Raw sugar futures in New York closed unchanged to higher in quiet trade. Benchmark July held steady at 11.45 cents/lb, while October added 5 points to close at 11.31 cents/lb. The July/October spread remained under pressure from commission house selling throughout the day. Speculators have begun to roll July positions into October ahead of the expiry of the July futures contract on June 30.

Traders said liquidation is expected to speed up after July options expire on June 13. Open interest in the front month remains heavy at 78,418 lots, up 715 lots as of early June 6. Traders said speculators tend to hold contracts until the week before expiry, when activity is likely to accelerate. In the Far East Thai raw sugar premiums firmed slightly on talk that Russia had entered the market and of further offtake by China.

The premium for July/August was quoted at 0.75/0.85 cents/lb compared with 0.65/0.75 cents/lb last week. However, this will be a temporary phenomenon only as up to 40 per cent of this year's raw sugar output has not yet been exported and traders are trying to find markets for a large part of that portion. Traders said the market is watching for any development of talk that China is expanding import licenses of raw sugar for tolling.

RUSSIA - Sugar beet sowings in Russia are still lagging behind. On June 2 beet sowings were 20 percent down on last year. The total area sown thus far was 902,000 ha or 85 percent of the total area planned.

GERMANY - Sugar imports in February 1997 amounted to 23,147 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 20,470 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first five months of 1996/97 (October/February) up to 101,329 tonnes compared to 92,379 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 206,911 tonnes compared to 225,848 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in October/February 1996/97 were France with 71,858 tonnes against 68,922 tonnes and the Netherlands with 9,930 tonnes compared to 6,953 tonnes.

Sugar exports in February 1997 reached 99,667 tonnes, down from 135,907 tonnes exported in February 1996. This brought cumulative exports in October/February 1996/97 up to 763,673 tonnes, slightly below the 788,357 tonnes exported the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 1.316 million tonnes against 1.452 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Italy with 106,792 tonnes whites against 34,033 tonnes, Belgium-Luxembourg with 100,011 tonnes against 101,318 tonnes, the United Arab Emirates with 93,548 tonnes, down from 99,220 tonnes and Switzerland with 42,083 tonnes against 48,300 tonnes.

SPAIN - Sugar imports in January 1997 amounted to 26,146 tonnes, down from 23,411 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first seven months of 1996/97 (July/January) up to 221,672 tonnes compared to 183,214 tonnes in 1995/96. Total imports in 1995/96 amounted to 353,193 tonnes against 257,273 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in 1996/97 were France with 125,360 tonnes whites against 106,100 tonnes and Germany with 36,696 tonnes, up from 30,058 tonnes.

Sugar exports in January 1997 reached 22,571 tonnes against 2,760 tonnes in January 1996. This brought cumulative exports in July/January 1996/97 up to 142,441 tonnes compared to 130,315 tonnes in 1995/96. Total exports in 1995/96 were 208,130 tonnes against 195,960 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Tunisia with 30,000 tonnes whites against 43,844 tonnes, Iran with 25,000 tonnes against nil and Syria with 23,001 tonnes against 3,000 tonnes.

UNITED KINGDOM - Sugar consumption in January 1997 amounted to 180,435 tonnes, raw value, sharply up on last year's 158,261 tonnes. This brought cumulative consumption in the first four months of 1996/97 (October/January) up to 768,679 tonnes, almost 80,000 tonnes up on the previous year's 692,826 tonnes. Total consumption in 1995/96 amounted to 2.333 million tonnes against 2.383 million tonnes in 1994/95.
